description: University of Texas at Austin and University of California San Diego researchers publish R code for evaluating commercial food-waste bans, with a linked Dryad dataset covering 36 US states during 1996–2019. The October 2025 Zenodo code release is free under MIT terms. It includes disposal comparisons, placebo tests, Monte Carlo calculations, composting and infrastructure analyses. These methods and inputs can calibrate waste-diversion scenarios or test policy assumptions in municipal-service simulations. The Dryad documentation defines disposal as state-generated municipal solid waste, excluding imports and including exports, and records corrections to material classification, trade adjustment, timing and missing-value handling. No related catalogue record explicitly covers the package. Older data versions are not interchangeable with corrected releases. Reported policy effects, reproducibility and uncertainty were not independently reassessed, and the code was not executed. DataCite confirms CC0 for the companion Dryad data, separately from the MIT code licence.
